holidays.name: Clean Up Your Room Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to tackling the avalanche of laundry, forgotten mugs, and mystery piles hiding in your bedroom. Participants are encouraged to dig out their floors and rediscover long-lost socks.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that appears on quirky holiday calendars as a playful nudge toward tidiness. It has no single known founder and spread through novelty calendars and social media.
holidays.funFact: Studies on household habits often find that people spend a surprising amount of time each year searching for misplaced items, so a good cleanup can be a real time saver.

holidays.name: National Shrimp Day
holidays.description: A salute to the beloved crustacean, celebrated with shrimp cocktail, scampi, tempura, shrimp tacos, and anything else that comes with a tail.
holidays.origin: A food holiday popularized in the United States by food-industry promotion and holiday calendars. Shrimp is the most popular seafood in America, which made it a natural candidate for its own day.
holidays.funFact: Shrimp have hearts located in their heads, and the average American eats several pounds of shrimp every year.

holidays.name: National Receptionists Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the people who greet visitors, answer the phones, and keep offices from descending into chaos. Think donuts, thank-you cards, and a heartfelt 'what would we do without you?'
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States, usually on the Wednesday of the last full week of April, though some calendars list related office appreciation days in May. It grew out of workplace appreciation traditions.
holidays.funFact: The switchboard operator was once among the most common jobs for young women in the early 20th century, and the receptionist role grew directly out of it.

holidays.name: Stay Up All Night Night
holidays.description: An unofficial night for burning the midnight oil with no regrets. Celebrate with movie marathons, board games, and enough snacks to power a small village until sunrise.
holidays.origin: A tongue-in-cheek observance from novelty holiday lists, designed as an excuse to stay awake just for the fun of it. Its exact creator is unknown.
holidays.funFact: The longest recorded time a person has voluntarily stayed awake is about 11 days, set by Randy Gardner in 1964, and doctors strongly advise against trying to beat it.
